source_meta._title: Horses, donkeys, mules and llamas spawned from spawn eggs or /summon command have 53 health

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft: Java Edition snapshot 20w15a, running in a new singleplayer Creative-mode world with cheats enabled. The instructions use keyboard-and-mouse default control names; use the corresponding bound controls if they have been changed.
preconditions: Use the first listed affected version, 20w15a, rather than the fix version 24w19a.
Configure the Minecraft Launcher to make historical Java Edition snapshots available and create or select an installation for exactly 20w15a.
Use a disposable test world because snapshots are development versions and should not be used to open an important existing world.
No world seed, coordinates, biome, difficulty, or world type is specified by the report.
The test requires permission to execute the report's /data command; enable cheats when creating the world.
Use only one horse for the query, and remain close to that horse so the selector sorted by nearest resolves to the intended entity.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher. If snapshot versions are not available, enable snapshots in the launcher installation settings. Create or select a Java Edition installation whose version is exactly 20w15a.
steps.success_cue: The selected launcher installation explicitly shows version 20w15a.

steps.action: Start the selected installation and wait for the Minecraft main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The main menu is responsive and its version text identifies the running game as Minecraft Java Edition 20w15a.

steps.action: Open the singleplayer world-creation screen by selecting Singleplayer and then Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Set Game Mode to Creative. This provides direct access to the Horse Spawn Egg without adding crafting or exploration to the reproduction.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows that Creative mode is selected.

steps.action: Set Allow Cheats to ON so that the report's /data command can be executed in chat.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows that cheats are enabled.

steps.action: Create the world. Do not enter a seed because the report does not specify one.
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned into the new world in Creative mode.

steps.action: Wait until nearby terrain has rendered and player movement and input respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The surrounding chunks are visible, and the player can move and look around without waiting for initial world loading.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory using the Inventory control.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory interface is open.

steps.action: Open the Search Items tab in the Creative inventory, focus its search field, and search for the horse spawn egg.
steps.success_cue: The search results include an item named Horse Spawn Egg.

steps.action: Move one Horse Spawn Egg from the search results into an empty hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots along the bottom of the inventory and gameplay screen.
steps.success_cue: A Horse Spawn Egg is present in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: Close the Creative inventory using the Inventory control or Escape.
steps.success_cue: Normal first-person gameplay is visible and the Horse Spawn Egg remains in the hotbar.

steps.action: Move to a clear patch of solid ground with enough open space for a horse. If a naturally generated horse is already nearby, move to another patch before continuing so the later nearest-horse selector is unambiguous.
steps.success_cue: There is solid ground within interaction reach, and no pre-existing horse is close to the player.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the Horse Spawn Egg using its number key or the mouse wheel. The selected slot is the active slot and has a visible highlight around it.
steps.exact_input: Hotbar key 1-9 corresponding to the Horse Spawn Egg slot
steps.success_cue: The Horse Spawn Egg is shown in the player's hand and its hotbar slot is highlighted.

steps.action: Aim the crosshair at the nearby solid ground and use the Horse Spawn Egg exactly once by pressing the Use Item/Place Block control.
steps.exact_input: Right mouse button (default Use Item/Place Block control)
steps.success_cue: Exactly one newly spawned horse is visible beside the targeted ground.

steps.action: Wait until the horse is fully visible, then stand within a few blocks of it. Do not spawn another horse, leave the world, or reload the world before querying its data.
steps.success_cue: The newly spawned horse is the nearest horse to the player, and normal movement and input remain responsive.

steps.action: Open the in-game chat input. The command must be executed in the current world by the player with cheats enabled, not entered into the launcher or a text editor.
steps.success_cue: The chat command input line is open at the bottom of the screen.

steps.action: Type the report's data query exactly as supplied, including the leading slash, selector arguments, capitalization of Health, and spaces. Do not modernize or otherwise modify the command.
steps.success_cue: The complete command is visible in the chat input line without a syntax error being shown before execution.

steps.action: Execute the command by pressing Enter once.
steps.success_cue: Chat displays a successful data-query result for the Health NBT path of the nearest horse. Stop immediately after this result appears and pass control to the observation subsystem without attacking, mounting, reloading, or respawning the horse.

stor.handoff_condition: The Horse Spawn Egg-created horse is still present as the nearest horse, and the exact /data get entity @e[type=horse,limit=1,sort=nearest] Health command has just produced its chat result. Begin observing and recording that returned Health value before any interaction or world reload changes the entity state.
uncertainties: The report provides formal reproduction steps only for a horse created with a spawn egg. Although the title and comments also mention donkeys, mules, llamas, and entities created with /summon, those variants are not added to this minimum reproduction path.
No seed, coordinates, biome, difficulty, or world type is specified. A new Creative world and a clear patch of solid ground are practical execution choices, not report-stated requirements.

The report does not specify whether other horses may be present. Keeping the spawned horse nearest to the player is added solely to ensure that the supplied nearest-entity selector queries the intended horse.
The report notes that leaving and re-entering can change the health state, so the plan avoids world reloads between spawning and querying; this ordering is supported by the supplied report comments.

External verification was used only to confirm snapshot availability workflow and the operational form of the Java Edition /data get entity command. The exact historical command from the report was preserved unchanged.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-184201:Villagers spawning too many Iron Golems | Duplicate:inward:MC-191903:Villagers gossip golem spawn | Duplicate:inward:MC-192391:Too many iron Golems spawning | Duplicate:inward:MC-192783:Way too many iron golems in their house | Duplicate:inward:MC-205895:Golem excessive overpopulation | Relates:outward:MC-158542:Iron Golems don't stop spawning | Relates:inward:MC-193217:Villagers don't reset their golem spawning timer when reloaded

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 20w19a, single-player integrated server, using the report attachment "2020-06-23_10-37-39_Village Test.zip". The attached test world is described as a Creative-mode, Peaceful-difficulty superflat world containing a villager trading-hall structure, villagers and beds, plus two iron golems buried underground. Run an unmodified vanilla client without gameplay-altering mods or additional data packs.
preconditions: Install and select an isolated Minecraft: Java Edition 20w19a launcher installation. In the official launcher, snapshot installations are exposed by enabling snapshots under the Installations tab. Use a separate game directory if possible so the imported test world cannot be opened accidentally in another version. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/en-us/article/minecraft-26-2-snapshot-2?utm_source=openai))

Obtain the exact Mojira attachment named "2020-06-23_10-37-39_Village Test.zip". The deterministic reload procedure depends on the prepared village and the two existing buried iron golems in this world.

Keep an untouched copy of the ZIP archive or extracted world before opening it. Snapshot versions can damage or irreversibly convert worlds, so each reproduction attempt should begin from a fresh copy. ([minecraft.net](https://www.minecraft.net/fr-ca/article/minecraft-snapshot-20w19a?utm_source=openai))

Commands must be available because the report requires changing the time. The attached world is described as Creative mode and should normally permit commands. If the imported world denies the command, temporarily enable commands through Esc -> Open to LAN -> Allow Cheats: ON -> Start LAN World, then retry the command.

Do not remove, kill, teleport, or uncover the two buried iron golems, and do not move or destroy the villagers, beds, or structure before triggering the reload. Their prepared state is part of the supplied test world.

steps.action: Close Minecraft completely. Extract a fresh copy of the report attachment "2020-06-23_10-37-39_Village Test.zip". Locate the extracted world directory—the directory that directly contains level.dat—and place that directory in the saves folder used by the isolated 20w19a installation. Avoid opening this copy in any newer Minecraft version first.
steps.success_cue: A single extracted world folder containing level.dat is present in the 20w19a installation's saves directory.

steps.action: Open the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation configured specifically for Java Edition snapshot 20w19a, and start the game. Confirm that the lower-left corner of the main menu identifies the running version as 20w19a before proceeding.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and displays version 20w19a.

steps.action: Click Singleplayer and select the imported test world created from the attachment. Do not select any similarly named working copy or an unrelated world.
steps.success_cue: The imported test world is highlighted in the world-selection list.

steps.action: Click Play Selected World to open the imported world. If Minecraft offers to create a backup, accept the backup or cancel and verify that the untouched archive is preserved before continuing; do not open the world in a different version.
steps.success_cue: The player has entered the imported superflat test world in 20w19a.

steps.action: Wait until the nearby terrain and constructed trading hall have rendered and player movement responds normally. Verify the loaded world matches the report: it is superflat, the player is in Creative mode, the difficulty is Peaceful, and a constructed enclosure or trading hall containing villagers and beds is present. Creative mode can be recognized by the absence of normal Survival health and hunger handling and by the ability to begin flying with a double-press of Space. Peaceful difficulty can be checked under Esc -> Options -> Difficulty without changing it.
steps.success_cue: The world is responsive, the villager structure is loaded, Creative mode is active, and Difficulty is set to Peaceful.

steps.action: Locate the villager trading-hall structure in the cleaned test world and move inside it, close enough that the villagers are visibly loaded and moving. If necessary in Creative mode, double-press Space to begin flying, use W/A/S/D to move, and press Space or Left Shift to move vertically. Land or stop flying inside the structure. Do not break blocks while entering.
steps.success_cue: The player is inside the structure and can see the loaded villagers and their beds or trading-hall area.

steps.action: Leave all entities and blocks in their prepared state. In particular, do not kill visible golems, dig down to inspect the two buried golems, move villagers, remove beds, or alter the structure. Remain inside or immediately adjacent to the villager area so its chunks stay loaded.
steps.success_cue: The villager area remains intact and loaded, with no entities or village blocks deliberately changed by the executor.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the executable Java Edition time command shown below, including the leading slash, and press Enter. The report writes the words as "/set time 09000", but Java Edition uses the "/time set" command order, so only the command-word order is corrected while the report's exact numeric argument 09000 is preserved. If an insufficient-permission error appears, press Esc, choose Open to LAN, set Allow Cheats to ON, choose Start LAN World, and then repeat this step.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that the time was set, and the world's daylight visibly changes to the time represented by 09000.

steps.action: Keep the villager structure loaded and wait for the villagers' gathering period to begin. Do not leave the area or advance the time again. Continue only when multiple villagers have begun moving toward or congregating around their shared gathering area, rather than merely standing at beds or workstations.
steps.success_cue: Multiple villagers are visibly in their gathering behavior or congregated in the common area while the structure remains loaded.

steps.action: As soon as the villagers are gathering, press Esc and click Save and Quit to Title. Do not wait through another villager schedule period before leaving.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Save and Quit to Title
steps.success_cue: The world has closed and the Minecraft title screen is visible.

steps.action: From the title screen, click Singleplayer and highlight the same imported test world that was just saved. Do not replace it with a new extraction between saving and reloading, because this step must reload the state established at time 09000.
steps.success_cue: The same test world used in the preceding steps is highlighted in the world-selection screen.

steps.action: Click Play Selected World once to reload that same world. This world reload is the report's trigger action; do not repeatedly click the button or open another world.
steps.success_cue: The loading screen begins for the same prepared test world.

steps.action: Wait only until the world and the villager structure have rendered and movement responds normally. Keep the structure's chunks loaded, do not kill or move any golem, and do not initiate another reload. Immediately transfer control to the observation subsystem once loading is complete.
steps.success_cue: The player is back in the responsive, fully rendered villager structure immediately after the time-09000 world reload.

stor.handoff_condition: The same prepared test world has just been reloaded after its villagers entered their gathering period at time 09000. The villager trading-hall chunks are fully rendered and responsive, and no villagers, beds, existing buried golems, newly present entities, or structure blocks have been altered after re-entry. Begin observation immediately.
uncertainties: The report attachment itself was not included as file content in the supplied prompt, so its spawn point, displayed world name, exact structure appearance, villager count, and precise locations of the two buried golems cannot be specified beyond the report's description.

The comments state that the original test village was created in 1.15.2 and tested in later snapshots, but they do not state the exact Minecraft version in which the attached cleaned backup was last saved. Because the first listed affected version must be used, this plan selects 20w19a. If 20w19a refuses to load the attachment as a newer-format save, preserve the failure and test from another untouched copy rather than manually downgrading world files.

The report gives the command as "/set time 09000". That word order is not executable Java Edition syntax; the plan uses "/time set 09000", preserving the supplied time argument. Minecraft command documentation identifies "/time set" as the applicable command form. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ACommand_blocks_and_functions?utm_source=openai))
The report does not give a fixed real-time wait duration for villagers to gather. The plan therefore uses visible villager congregation as the readiness condition rather than inventing a timeout.

The report says repeated reloads eventually make the structure overflow, but it also states that one reload reliably produces an additional spawn. This plan performs only one trigger cycle so the observation system can evaluate the minimum deterministic occurrence without intentionally creating excessive entities.

source_meta.issue links: Duplicate:inward:MC-241276:Pandas spawns rate are extremely low in the 1.18 first pre-release | Duplicate:inward:MC-241985:Pandas no longer spawn naturally | Relates:outward:MC-236756:Biome-exclusive mob spawn rates are reduced
source_meta._title: Pandas do not spawn in bamboo jungles with Default world

stor.environment: Minecraft: Java Edition 21w44a, vanilla single-player integrated server, fresh world with World Type set to Default. Creative mode is used as a practical aid for safe teleportation and terrain inspection; commands/cheats must be enabled. Do not use fix version 1.18 Pre-release 6.
preconditions: The Minecraft Launcher is configured to display historical snapshots, and the exact installation 21w44a is available.
Use an unmodified vanilla client: disable mods, custom datapacks, and server plugins that could change biome generation, entity spawning, commands, or entity visibility.
Create a new world directly in 21w44a; do not upgrade an existing world from another version.
Leave the world seed blank so Minecraft selects a seed, because the report supplies no deterministic seed.
Commands must be available to the player. In single-player, enable cheats while creating the world.
Keep the default doMobSpawning gamerule enabled. Do not summon pandas, kill existing passive mobs, or otherwise manipulate mob spawning before the test.
The target biome is specifically minecraft:bamboo_jungle, as identified by the title and the report's locate command; do not substitute an ordinary minecraft:jungle biome.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, create or select an installation whose Version field is the historical snapshot "21w44a", then launch the game with that installation. Confirm the version shown on the title screen before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft: Java Edition title screen is open and displays 21w44a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then select Create New World to open the world-creation screen.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is visible.

steps.action: Set Game Mode to Creative. Creative mode is not stated as a bug requirement; it is selected so the player can teleport above unknown terrain and descend safely without introducing survival preparation or fall damage.
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Game Mode: Creative.

steps.action: Open More World Options. Set World Type to Default, ensure Allow Cheats is ON, and leave the seed field blank. Do not choose Single Biome, Amplified, Large Biomes, or another world type.
steps.success_cue: World Type reads Default, commands are allowed, and no seed has been entered.

steps.action: Select Create New World and wait for world generation and player placement to finish.
steps.success_cue: The player is controllable in the newly generated world and the nearby terrain has rendered.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the gamerule query exactly as shown, including the leading slash, and press Enter. Do not change any other gamerules.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports that doMobSpawning is true. If it is false, this world does not have the required default spawning state; set it to true before continuing or recreate the world with default settings.

steps.action: Press T to open chat again. Enter the report's biome-location command exactly as shown, including the leading slash, then press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat reports the location of the nearest minecraft:bamboo_jungle and gives its horizontal X and Z coordinates and distance.

steps.action: Record the returned X coordinate and Z coordinate exactly, preserving any minus signs. In this affected version, /locatebiome identifies the target using horizontal coordinates; the teleport height will therefore be supplied separately.
steps.success_cue: The X and Z coordinates of the located bamboo jungle have been recorded and are available for the teleport command.

steps.action: Press T. Enter a teleport command using the recorded coordinates: replace <X_FROM_LOCATEBIOME> and <Z_FROM_LOCATEBIOME> with the returned integer values, omit the angle brackets, keep Y set to 200, include the leading slash, and press Enter. For example, coordinates X=-1200 and Z=640 would produce /tp @s -1200 200 640.
steps.success_cue: The player teleports to the located X/Z position at Y=200, and target-area terrain begins rendering below or around the player.

steps.action: Wait until the surrounding chunks have rendered and player movement responds normally. While in Creative flight, descend toward the terrain without dropping into Survival-style free fall. Stop above the bamboo canopy or on a safe exposed surface.
steps.success_cue: The terrain around the located position is fully visible, movement is responsive, and dense bamboo-jungle terrain can be approached safely.

steps.action: Open the debug screen with F3; on keyboards that reserve function keys, use the keyboard's equivalent such as Fn+F3. Read the biome entry and confirm that the player's current biome is minecraft:bamboo_jungle. If the player is immediately outside it, move horizontally toward the recorded locate position until the debug biome entry reads minecraft:bamboo_jungle.
steps.success_cue: The debug screen identifies the player's current biome as minecraft:bamboo_jungle.

steps.action: Close the debug screen with F3. Move through the bamboo jungle for approximately 64 to 128 horizontal blocks at a moderate Creative-flight or walking speed, staying near enough to the surface to inspect the terrain. Avoid attacking mobs, changing time, killing entities, summoning entities, or leaving the bamboo jungle. This traversal operationalizes the report's requirement to visit the biome and allows several target-biome chunks to load.
steps.success_cue: Several bamboo-jungle chunks have rendered around the player, bamboo-covered ground is visible, and movement remains responsive.

steps.action: Stop at a position still inside minecraft:bamboo_jungle and wait 60 seconds without using commands or leaving the biome. Keep the game unpaused so the integrated server continues ticking. The report does not define a waiting interval; this short interval provides a consistent opportunity for normal entity spawning before running its detection command.
steps.success_cue: The game has remained unpaused in a fully loaded bamboo-jungle area for 60 seconds.

steps.action: Press T to open chat. Enter the report's effect command exactly as written, including the leading slash, and press Enter once. Do not add a distance restriction, change the selector, or change the duration.
steps.success_cue: The command has been submitted, chat now contains its execution feedback, and any panda selected by the command would receive the glowing effect.

stor.handoff_condition: The player is in a loaded minecraft:bamboo_jungle in a fresh Default world, and /effect give @e[type=panda] glowing 1000 has just been executed once. Hand off immediately so the observation subsystem can inspect the command feedback and the loaded biome without any further movement, commands, entity spawning, or world modification.
uncertainties: The report supplies no seed or fixed coordinates, so /locatebiome determines a different target location for each generated world.
The report does not specify a game mode. Creative mode is selected only as a practical execution aid for commands, safe teleportation, flight, and terrain inspection.

The report does not explicitly state single-player versus dedicated server. A fresh single-player Default world is used because no dedicated-server, multiplayer, operator/non-operator, or server.properties condition is supplied.

The report does not define how much terrain must be loaded or how long the player must remain in the biome before executing the effect command. The 64-to-128-block traversal and 60-second unpaused interval are practical, bounded sampling choices rather than report-stated requirements.

The report calls @e[type=panda] a check for nearby pandas, but the supplied selector contains no distance limit. The exact report command is preserved and therefore targets matching loaded entities according to command-selector behavior.
Comments contain differing accounts of panda availability and rarity. Those claims are not converted into additional reproduction requirements.

Y=200 in the teleport command is a practical safety height because /locatebiome in the recommended affected version supplies the target's horizontal location rather than a terrain-safe destination height.

source_meta._title: Untamed cats on lead despawn when attached to fence post

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.18.1, unmodified vanilla client, single-player Creative-mode world using the integrated server. No Fabric, Forge, third-party server, datapack, or command is required. Control references assume default Java Edition key bindings unless they have been rebound.
preconditions: Install and select the exact Minecraft Java Edition version 1.18.1 in the launcher.
Use an unmodified vanilla installation and a single-player world in Creative mode, matching the environment in which the reporter confirmed the issue.
Use a test area with a clear, traversable line extending at least 100 horizontal blocks from the fence location. A flat, open area is preferred so the fence and cat can be viewed from a distance.

Set Render Distance and Simulation Distance high enough to keep terrain around the fence loaded at approximately 100 blocks; at least 8 chunks is a practical starting value. Keep Entity Distance at 100% or higher if that option has previously been reduced.
Have four available hotbar slots for an Oak Fence, Cat Spawn Egg, Lead, and Spyglass.
Do not feed fish to, otherwise tame, or use a name tag on the spawned cat. The target must remain an ordinary untamed cat.

steps.action: Start the game from the Minecraft Launcher using the installation configured for Java Edition 1.18.1. Do not launch a modded installation.
steps.success_cue: The main menu is displayed and identifies the running version as Minecraft Java Edition 1.18.1.

steps.action: Create a new single-player world in Creative mode, or load an existing unmodified single-player Creative world. Wait until terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a loaded single-player world and can use Creative flight and the Creative inventory.

steps.action: If necessary, open the pause menu and navigate to Options -> Video Settings. Set Render Distance and Simulation Distance to at least 8 chunks, and ensure Entity Distance is not below 100%. Return to the world after applying the settings.
steps.exact_input: Render Distance: at least 8 chunks; Simulation Distance: at least 8 chunks; Entity Distance: at least 100%
steps.success_cue: The world is active again with terrain visible for at least approximately 100 blocks in the intended travel direction.

steps.action: Locate a flat, open test area with a clear line of sight for at least 100 horizontal blocks. Avoid placing the test beside a cliff, dense forest, building, or other obstruction that would prevent looking back at the fence.
steps.success_cue: There is an unobstructed route and viewing line extending approximately 100 blocks from the selected fence location.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory, then open the Search Items tab identified by the magnifying-glass icon.
steps.success_cue: The Creative inventory is open and its item-search field is available.

steps.action: Click the search field, clear any existing text, enter "oak fence", and place one Oak Fence into hotbar slot 1. The report does not specify a wood type; Oak Fence is used as a representative fence post.
steps.success_cue: An Oak Fence is present in hotbar slot 1.

steps.action: Clear the inventory search field, enter "cat spawn egg", and place one Cat Spawn Egg into hotbar slot 2.
steps.success_cue: A Cat Spawn Egg is present in hotbar slot 2.

steps.action: Clear the inventory search field, enter "lead", and place one Lead into hotbar slot 3.
steps.success_cue: A Lead is present in hotbar slot 3.

steps.action: Clear the inventory search field, enter "spyglass", and place one Spyglass into hotbar slot 4. Close the inventory by pressing E.
steps.success_cue: A Spyglass is present in hotbar slot 4 and the player has returned to the world view.

steps.action: Select hotbar slot 1 using the 1 key, aim at the ground at the chosen test location, and right-click once to place the Oak Fence.
steps.success_cue: One freestanding vertical fence post is placed at the test location.

steps.action: Select hotbar slot 2 using the 2 key. Aim at the ground approximately 2 to 4 blocks from the fence and right-click once with the Cat Spawn Egg.
steps.success_cue: A live cat is visible close enough to the fence to be attached with a lead.

steps.action: Confirm that the spawned cat is untamed before continuing. It must not have a collar, and the player must not feed it raw cod or raw salmon. If it was accidentally tamed, spawn a fresh cat and use the fresh untamed cat instead.
steps.success_cue: The target cat is alive, has no collar, and has not been tamed or named.

steps.action: Select hotbar slot 3 using the 3 key. Approach until the cat is within interaction reach, center the crosshair on the cat, and right-click the cat once with the Lead. If the untamed cat moves away, follow it without feeding it and retry when it is within reach.
steps.success_cue: A lead line extends from the player to the untamed cat as the player moves away from it.

steps.action: While still holding the Lead, move within interaction reach of the fence post, center the crosshair on the fence, and right-click the fence once to tie the other end of the lead to it.
steps.success_cue: A lead knot is visible on the fence and the lead line runs between the fence and the untamed cat rather than between the cat and the player.

steps.action: Stand immediately beside the fence and press F3 to open the debug overlay. Record the displayed X and Z coordinates and choose one unobstructed horizontal direction in which to travel. Use the coordinate at the fence as the distance reference.
steps.success_cue: The starting X and Z coordinates near the fence have been recorded and a clear travel direction has been selected.

steps.action: Select the Spyglass in hotbar slot 4 before leaving the fence so it will already be in the active slot upon reaching the observation position.
steps.success_cue: The Spyglass is visible in the player's hand and is the active hotbar item.

steps.action: Enter Creative flight by pressing Space twice quickly. If necessary, hold Space briefly to rise only a few blocks above the ground while retaining an unobstructed view back toward the fence.
steps.exact_input: Double-tap Space; optionally hold Space briefly
steps.success_cue: The player is flying and can travel away without terrain or vegetation immediately blocking the return view.

steps.action: Fly promptly in a straight horizontal line away from the fence using the movement controls, normally W. Use the F3 coordinates to measure the displacement: continue until either X or Z differs from the recorded starting coordinate by approximately 100 blocks, preferably within 95 to 105 blocks. Do not travel diagonally unless calculating the total horizontal distance separately.
steps.exact_input: Hold W until the horizontal displacement is approximately 100 blocks
steps.success_cue: The player is stationary in flight approximately 100 horizontal blocks from the fence location.

steps.action: Release the movement controls and wait only until nearby terrain has finished rendering and movement responds normally. Do not fly back toward the fence, change dimensions, leave the world, or use commands that move the player or the cat.
steps.success_cue: The player remains approximately 100 blocks from the fence, the relevant terrain is rendered, and input is responsive.

steps.action: Turn to face the recorded fence location. With the Spyglass still selected, hold the Use Item control, which is right-click by default, and center the magnified view on the fence and tethered-cat area.
steps.exact_input: Right-click and hold while aiming at the fence location
steps.success_cue: The circular spyglass zoom overlay is visible and the fence-and-cat test area is centered in the magnified view at the beginning of the observation interval.

steps.action: Begin a 120-second observation interval while remaining approximately 100 blocks from the fence. Keep the spyglass view aimed at the test area as continuously as practical, and do not approach or interact with the cat or fence during this interval. Hand control to the observation subsystem as soon as the interval starts.
steps.exact_input: Maintain approximately 100-block distance for up to 120 seconds
steps.success_cue: The timer has started, the player remains at the required distance, and the spyglass is directed toward the tethered-cat test area without any further setup action pending.

stor.handoff_condition: The untamed cat is tied by a lead to the fence, the player is stationary approximately 100 horizontal blocks away, the test area is centered through the spyglass, and the 120-second distant-observation interval has just started. The observation subsystem should now monitor the cat, lead, and fence area without moving the player closer or interacting with the setup.
uncertainties: The report gives no world seed, biome, difficulty, cat variant, or precise fence wood type. These are treated as nonessential; Oak Fence and any clear Creative-world location are used as practical choices.
The instruction says to move "about 100 blocks away" rather than giving an exact threshold. This plan operationalizes that as a horizontal distance of approximately 95 to 105 blocks from the fence.
The report gives a variable interval of 15 to 120 seconds rather than one exact delay. The plan therefore starts a full 120-second observation window.
The description mentions both untamed cats and ocelots, but the title and numbered reproduction instructions specifically use a wild cat. This plan reproduces the cat case only.

The minimum Render Distance, Simulation Distance, and Entity Distance values are not stated in the report. The suggested values are practical measures intended to keep the test location rendered and observable at approximately 100 blocks.

The bug is distance-and-time dependent rather than being initiated by one instantaneous interaction. Step 21 is designated as the trigger because it begins the sustained distant interval after all required setup conditions have been established.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:inward:MC-302842:Nautiluses and zombie nautiluses never despawn
source_meta._title: Zombie nautiluses generated in ocean ruins are not persistent

stor.environment: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.11 Release Candidate 2 in a newly created singleplayer world using the integrated server. Use Creative mode with commands enabled, a non-Peaceful difficulty such as the default Normal difficulty, and a render distance of at least 8 chunks.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact affected version: Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.11 Release Candidate 2. Do not use the fix version, 1.21.11 Release Candidate 3.
Use a newly created world so the target ocean-ruin chunks have not already been generated or visited in this save.
Use the exact seed -8790581265353131111.
Enable commands for the world. Creative mode is recommended so the player can safely remain underwater and use all required teleport commands without Survival hazards interfering.
Set Render Distance to 8 chunks or greater before generating the target area.
Do not name, mount, leash, place in a boat, or otherwise interact with the target zombie nautilus, because such actions could change its persistence or behavior.
Keep the world difficulty above Peaceful so hostile mobs are not removed for an unrelated reason.

steps.action: Launch Minecraft Java Edition using the installation for version 1.21.11 Release Candidate 2, then wait for the main menu to finish loading.
steps.success_cue: The lower-left version label on the main menu identifies the running version as 1.21.11 Release Candidate 2.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, set Game Mode to Creative, and ensure commands are enabled. Open the world-generation settings, enter the report's seed exactly, and create the world.
steps.success_cue: A new Creative singleplayer world opens and the player can move normally.

steps.action: Confirm that the difficulty is not Peaceful. If necessary, press Esc, select Options, open Difficulty, and choose Normal or another non-Peaceful difficulty.
steps.success_cue: The active difficulty is Easy, Normal, or Hard rather than Peaceful.

steps.action: Set the render distance to at least 8 chunks: press Esc, select Options, select Video Settings, adjust Render Distance to 8 chunks or greater, and select Done until returning to the world.
steps.success_cue: The Video Settings screen shows Render Distance set to 8 chunks or greater, and the player has returned to gameplay.

steps.action: Wait before teleporting until the initial spawn terrain has rendered and movement and commands respond normally.
steps.success_cue: Nearby chunks are visible, the loading screen is gone, and player movement responds without world-loading pauses.

steps.action: Teleport to the report's target coordinates. Press T to open in-game chat, enter the command exactly with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The teleport completes and the player is at approximately X=-9591, Y=63, Z=8825. Ocean terrain begins rendering around the destination.

steps.action: Do not issue another command yet. Wait until the destination chunks, including the nearby ocean-ruin area, have rendered and player movement and commands respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The surrounding ocean terrain is loaded, no terrain-loading screen remains, and the player can move normally at the destination.

steps.action: Locate the nearest generated zombie nautilus using the report's selector. Press T, enter the command exactly with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The command teleports the player to a zombie nautilus associated with the ocean-ruin area. If the command instead reports that no entity was found, the required setup state was not reached; stop and retry in another newly created world using the same version, seed, settings, and sequence.

steps.action: Allow the immediate surroundings at the zombie nautilus to finish rendering. Do not interact with, name, mount, attack, or otherwise modify the zombie nautilus.
steps.success_cue: The player is beside the zombie nautilus, the nearby ocean-ruin terrain is loaded, and the entity has not been altered by player interaction.

steps.action: Teleport vertically to absolute Y=256 while retaining the current X and Z coordinates. Press T, enter the report's command exactly, and press Enter. The number 256 is an absolute Y coordinate because it does not have a tilde; do not change this to /tp ~ ~256 ~.
steps.success_cue: The teleport completes. The player remains at the same horizontal X and Z location and is now at approximately Y=256.

steps.action: Wait until the high-altitude teleport has completed and movement and commands respond normally before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The player is stable at approximately Y=256, the loading transition is finished, and chat commands can be entered normally.

steps.action: Teleport back to absolute Y=64 at the same X and Z coordinates. Press T, enter the report's command exactly, and press Enter. The number 64 is an absolute Y coordinate; do not change this to a relative vertical movement.
steps.success_cue: The teleport completes. The player is at approximately Y=64 at the same horizontal location, and the surrounding ocean chunks have rendered enough for commands to respond normally.

steps.action: Run the nearest-zombie-nautilus teleport command a second time. Press T, enter the command exactly with its leading slash, press Enter once, and immediately hand control to the observation subsystem without issuing additional commands.
steps.success_cue: The second nearest-zombie-nautilus command has been submitted, and its resulting chat response and any resulting player teleport are available for the observation subsystem to inspect.

stor.handoff_condition: The second `/tp @n[type=zombie_nautilus]` command has just been submitted after the player moved from the ocean ruin to absolute Y=256 and back to absolute Y=64. Begin observing the command response and player destination immediately, without performing another action.
uncertainties: A report comment states that one tester did not find a zombie nautilus at the primary coordinates and instead found one near /tp -7326 46 6539; the main report's seed and coordinates remain the primary reproduction path and the alternate location has not been substituted.

The report does not explicitly state game mode or difficulty. Creative mode, commands enabled, and a non-Peaceful difficulty are practical setup choices intended to execute the supplied commands safely without removing the target for an unrelated reason.
The report says render distance 8 or more but does not specify simulation distance, so no simulation-distance requirement has been added.

If the first `/tp @n[type=zombie_nautilus]` lookup fails, the subsequent steps do not establish this report's required precondition. A fresh world retry is preferred over continuing or manually summoning a replacement, because the bug specifically concerns a zombie nautilus generated as part of an ocean ruin.
